content.text: The verifier's narrative confirms the compliant classification is correct; the only failing item is the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check, which it expressly identifies as an expected artefact where no audit clause exists. I will re-submit the same finding, making that point explicit in the rationale, with no redline.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: No issue: the AUDIT rule has no target in this agreement. There is no usage-, metering- or licence-compliance audit right binding Customer — no clause uses audit, inspect, verify, examine or records-access language against us; § 4.1/4.2 (p0052) have IBM meter and invoice its own usage Charges with no verification right against Customer's books; and § 12.1 grants the Base Components licence with no compliance-verification right. The only inspection-flavoured provision, § 11.3 (p0132), is an abuse/acceptable-use enforcement right — IBM investigating suspected breaches of the content warranties in § 11.2(b) — i.e. a security and illegal-content mechanism, not a commercial audit, with p0137's emergency/required-by-law notice standard and p0138's information obligation as its counterparts. Because an audit right against Customer is inherently adverse to us, its absence is more favourable than the playbook preferred position, so this is compliant rather than a missing-protection deviation, and no redline is warranted. The failing deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is an expected artefact of there being no audit clause to parameterise, not a defect: grafting frequency, notice, a 5% underpayment cost-shift and a no-systems-access bar onto the abuse-investigation clause would contradict p0137's emergency carve-out and p0138, bar IBM from responding to a second security or abuse incident, and import an inoperative payment trigger in a hosting deal where IBM operates the environment. Flagged for follow-up: apply the AUDIT parameters if a Service Option Attachment or Order Form later introduces usage verification.
